SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: EYE-HAND COORDINATION SKILLS
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Eye-hand coordination skills helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: EYE-HAND COORDINATION SKILLS
Study Eye-hand coordination skills like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate eye-hand cutting paper along a marked line and for preparing a

What this means
In this part you learn to Demonstrate eye-hand cutting paper along a marked line and for preparing a. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Demonstrate eye-hand cutting paper along a marked line and for preparing a.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Eye-hand coordination skills”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Demonstrate eye-hand cutting paper along a marked line and for preparing a. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Eye-hand coordination skills is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Eye-hand coordination skills”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Demonstrate eye-hand cutting paper along a marked line and for preparing a)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Eye-hand coordination skills to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Demonstrate eye-hand cutting paper along a marked line and for preparing a.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Eye-hand coordination skills from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Eye-hand coordination skills: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Eye-hand coordination skills?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Eye-hand coordination skills means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Demonstrate eye-hand cutting paper along a marked line and for preparing a.
